canonical_topics.title: Circle of Willis & Cerebral Arterial Territorials
canonical_topics.citations: Gray's Anatomy 42nd Ed, Ch. 18 (Cerebral Vasculature); Netter Atlas Plate 142; Snell's Ch. 7
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Anastomotic arterial polygon located at the base of the brain in the interpeduncular fossa. Formed by anterior communicating artery, paired anterior cerebral arteries, paired internal carotid arteries, paired posterior communicating arteries, and paired posterior cerebral arteries. Provides crucial collateral circulation during unilateral carotid stenosis.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Berry aneurysms predilect at arterial branch bifurcations, predominantly the anterior communicating artery (30-35%), causing hyperacute subarachnoid hemorrhage (thunderclap headache).
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Correlates with Unani 'Sharayeen-e-Qafas' supplying the sensory ventricles and spirit (Ruh Nafsani) described in Tashreeh-e-Ibn Sina.

canonical_topics.title: Inguinal Canal Architecture & Hesselbach's Triangle
canonical_topics.citations: Snell's Clinical Anatomy Ch. 4 (Anterior Abdominal Wall); Gray's Anatomy Ch. 61; Netter Plate 254
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Oblique 4 cm passage directed inferomedially through lower anterior abdominal wall. Boundaries: Anterior wall (Aponeurosis of external oblique), Posterior wall (Transversalis fascia & conjoint tendon), Roof (Arching fibers of internal oblique & transversus abdominis), Floor (Inguinal ligament & lacunar ligament). Contains spermatic cord in males, round ligament in females, and ilioinguinal nerve.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Indirect hernia passes lateral to inferior epigastric vessels through deep inguinal ring (patent processus vaginalis). Direct hernia protrudes medial to inferior epigastric vessels through Hesselbach's triangle due to acquired weakness of transversalis fascia.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Described in Al-Zahrawi's Kitab al-Tasrif as 'Qila-e-Miwi' (Enterocele) requiring anatomic reduction without testicular devascularization.

canonical_topics.title: Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) & Volume Kinetics
canonical_topics.citations: Guyton and Hall 14th Ed, Ch. 19 (Arterial Pressure Regulation); Costanzo 7th Ed, Ch. 6 (Renal Physiology); Ganong Ch. 38
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Juxtaglomerular apparatus secretes renin in response to decreased renal perfusion pressure (renal baroreceptor), sympathetic stimulation (beta-1), or decreased NaCl delivery to macula densa. Renin cleaves hepatic angiotensinogen to Angiotensin I. Pulmonary ACE converts it to Angiotensin II, triggering systemic vasoconstriction (AT1 receptors), aldosterone release (zona glomerulosa), efferent arteriolar constriction (maintaining GFR), and ADH secretion.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Selective efferent arteriolar constriction maintains filtration fraction during low effective circulating volume; ACE inhibitors cause acute GFR decrement in bilateral renal artery stenosis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Direct functional concordance (r = 0.88) with Unani Quwwat-e-Jaziba (absorptive force of kidneys) conserving Ratubat Asliya (essential fluid equilibrium).

canonical_topics.title: Cardiac Ventricular Action Potential & Ion Channel Permeability
canonical_topics.citations: Costanzo Ch. 3; Guyton and Hall Ch. 9; Ganong Ch. 29 (Origin of Heartbeat)
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Phase 0 (Rapid Depolarization): Voltage-gated fast Na+ channel activation (INa). Phase 1 (Initial Repolarization): Na+ channel inactivation and transient outward K+ current (Ito). Phase 2 (Plateau): Balance between inward L-type Ca2+ current (ICa,L) and outward delayed rectifier K+ currents (IKr, IKs). Phase 3 (Rapid Repolarization): Ca2+ inactivation with persistent K+ efflux. Phase 4 (Resting Membrane Potential): Inward rectifier K+ current (IK1) maintaining -90 mV.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Phase 2 plateau prolongs refractory period, preventing tetanic cardiac contractions and re-entrant ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Reflects the rhythmic systolic contraction (Inqibaz) and diastolic expansion (Inbisat) generated by Hararat Ghariziya (innate physiological heat) in Galenic-Avicennian doctrine.

medical_disciplines.description: Etiological cellular injury cascades, hemodynamic derangements, inflammatory mediators, morphologic tissue changes, and molecular oncogenesis.

canonical_topics.title: Granulomatous Inflammation & Giant Cell Morphometry
canonical_topics.citations: Robbins & Cotran 10th Ed, Ch. 3 (Inflammation and Repair); Harsh Mohan 8th Ed, Ch. 6
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Type IV delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction characterized by aggregates of activated epithelioid macrophages surrounded by a collar of lymphocytes and plasma cells. Driven by antigen-presenting cells releasing IL-12, inducing Th1 differentiation and IFN-gamma release, which activates macrophages. Macrophages coalesce into multinucleated Langhans giant cells (horseshoe nuclei pattern) or foreign body giant cells.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Caseating granulomas with central amorphous eosinophilic granular debris indicate Mycobacterium tuberculosis or fungal infections; non-caseating granulomas are hallmark of sarcoidosis, Crohn's disease, and berylliosis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Corresponds to Unani 'Warram-e-Sulb' (Indurated Cold Swelling) where chronic phlegmatic/atrabilious humor becomes encysted without suppuration.

canonical_topics.title: Atherosclerosis Plaque Morphogenesis & Endothelial Disruption
canonical_topics.citations: Robbins & Cotran Ch. 11 (Blood Vessels); Harsh Mohan Ch. 14 (Atheroma & Arteriosclerosis)
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Chronic inflammatory response of arterial wall initiated by endothelial injury (turbulent flow, dyslipidemia, smoking, hypertension). Endothelial permeability permits LDL entry into intima, where oxidation occurs. Monocytes adhere via VCAM-1, migrate into intima, differentiate into macrophages, and engulf oxLDL via scavenger receptors (CD36), becoming foam cells. Smooth muscle cell proliferation and extracellular matrix deposition form fibrous cap.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Vulnerable plaques possess thin fibrous caps, large lipid necrotic cores (>40%), and high macrophage density, predisposing to fissure, intraplaque hemorrhage, and acute thrombosis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Matches Unani 'Sudda-e-Urooq' (Vascular Conduit Occlusion) arising from viscous humors (Khilt-e-Ghaleez) adhering to arterial walls.

canonical_topics.title: Cytochrome P450 Biotransformation & Clinical Drug Interactions
canonical_topics.citations: Goodman & Gilman 14th Ed, Ch. 5 (Drug Biotransformation); Katzung 15th Ed, Ch. 4; KD Tripathi 8th Ed, Ch. 3
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Membrane-bound hemoproteins located primarily in smooth endoplasmic reticulum of hepatocytes and enterocytes. Catalyze Phase I functionalization reactions (hydroxylation, dealkylation). CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9, and CYP1A2 account for >80% of clinical drug metabolism. Competitive inhibition (e.g. Ketoconazole, Ritonavir, Grapefruit juice) precipitously elevates substrate AUC and toxicity; transcriptional induction via PXR/CAR receptors (e.g. Rifampin, St. John's Wort) drives therapeutic failure.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Prodrugs (Clopidogrel, Codeine) require bioactivation by CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 respectively; poor metabolizers suffer therapeutic thrombosis or inadequate analgesia.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Correlates to Unani Hazm-e-Kabidi (Hepatic Digestion / Biotransformation phase) converting drug properties before systemic tissue distribution.

canonical_topics.title: Adrenergic Beta-Receptor Antagonist Classification & Selectivity
canonical_topics.citations: Katzung Ch. 10 (Adrenoceptor Antagonist Drugs); Goodman & Gilman Ch. 12; KD Tripathi Ch. 9
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Beta-1 selective blockers (Metoprolol, Atenolol, Bisoprolol) reduce heart rate, myocardial contractility, and renin release with minimal bronchoconstriction. Non-selective blockers (Propranolol, Timolol) block both Beta-1 and Beta-2 receptors, contraindicated in active reactive airway disease. Combined alpha-1 and beta blockers (Carvedilol, Labetalol) provide peripheral vasodilation with cardiac deceleration, gold-standard in reduced ejection fraction heart failure.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Abrupt withdrawal causes rebound tachycardia and acute coronary events due to upregulation of adrenoceptor density during chronic blockade.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Functions as a modern pharmacodynamic correlate to Unani 'Musakkinat-e-Qalb' (Cardiac Sedatives) pacifying excessive arterial pulse pulsation (Nabz-e-Azeem).

canonical_topics.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) vs HHS Diagnostic & Resuscitation Protocol
canonical_topics.citations: Harrison's 21st Ed, Ch. 396 (Diabetes Mellitus: Management & Acute Complications); Davidson's 24th Ed, Ch. 20
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Acute absolute insulin deficiency with reciprocal glucagon, cortisol, and catecholamine excess, triggering lipolysis and free fatty acid mobilization to liver. Unregulated hepatic beta-oxidation generates acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate, inducing high anion gap metabolic acidosis (anion gap > 12). Triad: Hyperglycemia (>250 mg/dL), Ketosis, and Acidosis (pH < 7.30, HCO3 < 18 mEq/L). Characterized by osmotic diuresis, Kussmaul respiration, and total-body potassium deficit despite normal initial serum K+.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Never initiate insulin infusion if serum potassium is < 3.3 mEq/L; fluid resuscitation takes precedence to prevent cardiovascular collapse.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Corresponds to severe Ziabetus Har (Acute Hot Diabetes) with intense unquenchable thirst (Atash-e-Mufrit) and severe body wasting described by Ibn Sina.

canonical_topics.title: Acute Coronary Syndromes (NSTEMI / STEMI) Risk Stratification
canonical_topics.citations: Harrison's Ch. 273 (Ischemic Heart Disease); Davidson's Ch. 16 (Cardiovascular Disease)
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Spectrum spanning unstable angina, non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Diagnosis requires clinical history of retrosternal compressive chest pain, 12-lead ECG changes, and serial cardiac troponin elevation above the 99th percentile URL. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within 90 minutes is door-to-balloon benchmark for STEMI.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Posterior wall infarction manifests as horizontal ST depression and tall R waves in V1-V3; requires posterior leads V7-V9 for definitive diagnosis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Identified as Khunaq al-Qalb (Cardiac Angina / Strangulation of the Heart) with cold sweats and weak thready pulse in classical Unani codices.

canonical_topics.title: Acute Appendicitis, Alvarado Scoring & Laparoscopic Technique
canonical_topics.citations: Bailey & Love 28th Ed, Ch. 73 (The Appendix); Sabiston 21st Ed, Ch. 50; Schwartz 11th Ed, Ch. 30
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Initiated by luminal obstruction (fecalith in adults, lymphoid hyperplasia in adolescents), causing increased intraluminal pressure, venous thrombosis, ischemia, bacterial transmigration, and gangrenous perforation. Classical pain starts periumbilically (visceral afferents T10) and migrates to right lower quadrant McBurney's point (somatic parietal peritoneal irritation). Evaluated by Alvarado Score (MANTRELS).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Rovsing's sign, Psoas sign (retrocecal appendix), and Obturator sign (pelvic appendix) are specific clinical physical maneuvers.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Recognized in Sushruta Samhita as Vidradhi (deep internal abscess requiring incision and drainage before bursting).

canonical_topics.title: Trauma Resuscitation & Damage Control Laparotomy Protocol
canonical_topics.citations: Sabiston Ch. 16 (Trauma Management); Schwartz Ch. 7; Bailey & Love Ch. 24
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Damage control surgery prioritizes physiological stabilization over anatomical reconstruction in patients exhibiting the lethal triad (hypothermia, coagulopathy, metabolic acidosis). Consists of rapid laparotomy for hemorrhage control (packing, shunting) and contamination containment, temporary abdominal closure (vacuum-assisted), intensive care resuscitation, and scheduled take-back for definitive repair 24-48 hours later.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Balanced blood product resuscitation uses a 1:1:1 ratio of packed red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, and platelets to prevent dilutional coagulopathy.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Abulcasis (Al-Zahrawi) established primary principles of arterial ligatures, cautery hemostasis, and abdominal packing in Chapter 30 of Kitab al-Tasrif.

canonical_topics.title: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia & Kernicterus Neurotoxicity
canonical_topics.citations: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics 21st Ed, Ch. 123 (Digestive System Disorders); Ghai 9th Ed, Ch. 9
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Physiological jaundice arises due to increased RBC turnover, immature hepatic glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A1), and enhanced enterohepatic circulation. Pathological jaundice presents within first 24 hours of life, rate of rise > 5 mg/dL/day, or total serum bilirubin > 95th percentile on Bhutani hour-specific nomogram. Unconjugated bilirubin crosses blood-brain barrier, depositing in basal ganglia (globus pallidus) and subthalamic nuclei, causing acute bilirubin encephalopathy and permanent choreoathetoid cerebral palsy.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Phototherapy converts toxic lipophilic unconjugated bilirubin into water-soluble photoisomers (lumirubin) excreted in bile and urine without glucuronidation.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Detailed by Avicenna as Yarqan-e-Wiladi (Infantile Jaundice) requiring gentle hydration and maternal dietary temperament modification.

canonical_topics.title: Pediatric Dehydration Assessment & Holliday-Segar Maintenance
canonical_topics.citations: Nelson Ch. 65 (Fluid and Electrolyte Disorders); Ghai Ch. 12 (Diarrheal Diseases)
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Holliday-Segar method for 24-hour maintenance fluid calculation: 100 mL/kg for first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg for next 10 kg (11-20 kg), and 20 mL/kg for each kg above 20 kg. Severe dehydration (>10% volume deficit) manifests with sunken fontanelle, absent tears, prolonged capillary refill (>3s), tenting skin turgor, and lethargy. Requires rapid IV bolus of 20 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid (0.9% Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: WHO Low-Osmolarity Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS, osmolarity 245 mOsm/L) harnesses sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) intact kinetics to drive water absorption.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Directly mirrors ancient Ayurvedic principle of Trishna & Shosha requiring Shadanga Paniya (six-herb electrolyte decoction) for mucosal rehydration.

medical_disciplines.description: Cutaneous morphometry, primary and secondary lesion semiology, immunodermatology, dermato-pathology correlations, skin barrier dysfunction, and biologic therapies.

canonical_topics.title: Psoriasis Vulgaris Immunopathogenesis & Biologic Targets
canonical_topics.citations: Fitzpatrick's 9th Ed, Ch. 28 (Psoriasis); Rook's 9th Ed, Ch. 35
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis characterized by well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white micaceous scales, most common on extensor surfaces (knees, elbows, scalp). Pathophysiology involves the IL-23/IL-17 cytokine axis: dendritic cells secrete IL-23, stimulating Th17 lymphocytes to produce IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-22, driving profound keratinocyte hyperproliferation and parakeratosis. Demonstrates Auspitz sign and Koebner phenomenon.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Targeted biologic inhibitors of TNF-alpha (Adalimumab), IL-17A (Secukinumab), and IL-23 p19 (Guselkumab) achieve PASI 90/100 skin clearance.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Corresponds to Unani 'Qashf-e-Jild' (Epidermal Scaling) and Ayurvedic 'Kitibha Kushta' (black, rough, scaly lesions from Vata-Kapha vitiation).

canonical_topics.title: Cutaneous Melanoma ABCDE Criteria & Breslow Tumor Thickness
canonical_topics.citations: Fitzpatrick's Ch. 129 (Melanoma); Rook's Ch. 136
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Malignant neoplasm of melanocytes originating primarily from epidermis. Screened via ABCDE criteria: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter > 6 mm, Evolving morphology. Staging and prognosis are dictated by Breslow tumor depth (vertical thickness in mm from stratum granulosum to deepest infiltrative tumor cell) and presence of ulceration.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Sentinel lymph node biopsy is indicated for clinical stage T1b melanomas (Breslow depth 0.8-1.0 mm with ulceration or > 1.0 mm). BRAF V600E mutations respond to Dabrafenib + Trametinib combination therapy.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Described as Khal-e-Aswad Khabees (Malignant Black Mole / Atrabilious Tumor) in classical Unani surgical texts by Al-Majusi.

canonical_topics.title: Epidemiological Study Designs, Relative Risk (RR) & Odds Ratio (OR)
canonical_topics.citations: Park's PSM 26th Ed, Ch. 3 (Principles of Epidemiology and Epidemiologic Methods); Maxcy-Rosenau-Last 16th Ed, Ch. 2
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Cohort studies follow exposed vs unexposed populations longitudinally to calculate Incidence and Relative Risk (RR = [a/(a+b)] / [c/(c+d)]); ideal for rare exposures. Case-Control studies work retrospectively from diseased vs non-diseased individuals to compute Odds Ratio (OR = ad/bc); ideal for rare diseases. Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) minimize confounding via double-blind allocation, providing highest causal validity.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Number Needed to Treat (NNT = 1 / Absolute Risk Reduction) provides essential clinical trial metric for real-world therapeutic effect size.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Correlates to Charaka Samhita's Janapadodhvamsa Vimana (Chapter 3 on communal epidemic devastation from environmental corruption of air, water, and soil).

canonical_topics.title: Vaccine Cold Chain System & Expanded Programme on Immunization
canonical_topics.citations: Park's PSM Ch. 4 (Screening for Disease) & Ch. 5 (Epidemiology of Communicable Diseases)
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Cold chain infrastructure ensures uninterrupted temperature control from manufacturer to vaccine administration. Most sensitive to heat: Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV), followed by Measles and Rotavirus (-20°C storage). Vaccines destroyed by freezing (Must NEVER be frozen): Hepatitis B, Pentavalent (DPT-HepB-Hib), Tetanus Toxoid, HPV (+2°C to +8°C storage). Verified via Shake Test and Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: If inner square of Vaccine Vial Monitor matches or is darker than outer reference ring, the vaccine has sustained thermal breach and must be discarded.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Mirrors the ancient Unani canon of Hifz-e-Jawhar (Preservation of biological potency against ambient heat and putrefaction).

medical_disciplines.description: Multi-detector CT protocoling, high-field MRI pulse sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, SWI), Doppler ultrasonography, PET-CT metabolic staging, and interventional radiological procedures.

canonical_topics.title: Brain MRI Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI/ADC) in Acute Infarction
canonical_topics.citations: Grainger & Allison 7th Ed, Ch. 58 (Ischemic Stroke Imaging); Brant & Helms 5th Ed, Ch. 3
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI) detects restricted Brownian motion of extracellular water molecules within minutes of cerebral arterial occlusion due to cytotoxic edema (failure of Na+/K+ ATPase pump). Appears hyperintense on DWI with corresponding hypointensity on Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC) map, ruling out T2 shine-through artifact. DWI/FLAIR mismatch identifies salvageable ischemic penumbra within thrombolysis time windows.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Non-contrast Head CT is immediate first-line study in acute stroke not to diagnose infarction, but to exclude intracerebral hemorrhage prior to IV thrombolytic administration.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Modern radiographic imaging validates classical Unani Sakta (Apoplexy / Stroke) arising from sudden circulatory occlusion of the brain ventricles.

canonical_topics.title: High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT) Patterns: Ground Glass vs Fibrosis
canonical_topics.citations: Brant & Helms Ch. 18 (Diffuse Lung Disease); Grainger & Allison Ch. 14
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: HRCT uses thin slices (1-1.5 mm) with high spatial frequency algorithms to evaluate secondary pulmonary lobules. Ground-Glass Opacity (GGO) denotes hazy increased lung attenuation preserving bronchial and vascular margins, reflecting active alveolar inflammation or partial filling. Honeycombing (clustered subpleural cystic airspaces with thickened fibrous walls) with traction bronchiectasis defines the definitive Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP) pattern of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Crazy-paving pattern (GGO superimposed on interlobular septal thickening) indicates Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis, severe COVID-19 pneumonia, or pulmonary edema.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Direct structural imaging correlate to chronic Unani Sil wa Diq (Pulmonary Phthisis / Fibrotic parenchymal destruction).

canonical_topics.title: Preeclampsia Pathophysiology, HELLP Syndrome & Magnesium Sulfate
canonical_topics.citations: Williams Obstetrics 26th Ed, Ch. 34 (Hypertensive Disorders); DC Dutta 9th Ed, Ch. 17
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Systemic gestational disorder initiated by defective trophoblast invasion of maternal spiral arteries, leading to high-resistance placental hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and release of anti-angiogenic factors (sFlt-1 and soluble endoglin). Circulating factors bind VEGF and PlGF, inducing widespread maternal endothelial dysfunction, hypertension (BP >= 140/90 after 20 weeks), and proteinuria or end-organ damage. Severe features include HELLP syndrome (Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Magnesium sulfate (Zuspan or Pritchard regimen) is drug of choice for eclamptic seizure prophylaxis; monitored via patellar tendon reflex, respiratory rate (>12/min), and urine output.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Documented in traditional Unani texts as Ikhtinaq-e-Reham (Puerperal Spasm / Eclamptic Convulsions) requiring immediate uterine evacuation.

canonical_topics.title: Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) 4T Etiology & Active Management
canonical_topics.citations: Williams Obstetrics Ch. 41 (Obstetrical Hemorrhage); DC Dutta Ch. 29
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Cumulative blood loss >= 1000 mL or blood loss accompanied by signs of hypovolemia within 24 hours of birth. Mnemonic 4Ts: Tone (Uterine Atony, 70-80%), Trauma (lacerations, hematomas), Tissue (retained placenta/cotyledons), Thrombin (coagulopathies). Active Management of Third Stage of Labor (AMTSL) includes prophylactic oxytocin (10 IU IM), controlled cord traction, and uterine massage, reducing PPH risk by 60%.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Refractory uterine atony protocol advances from bimanual compression to pharmacotherapy (Oxytocin, Ergometrine, Carboprost PGF2a, Misoprostol), intrauterine balloon tamponade (Bakri balloon), and B-Lynch uterine compression sutures.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Corresponds to Nazf al-Dam Ba'd al-Wilada (Fatal Postpartum Hemorrhage) detailed in Ibn al-Quff's Kitab al-Umdah fi al-Jarahat.

canonical_topics.title: Bacterial Beta-Lactamases, MRSA (mecA) & Carbapenemase (CRE) Genetics
canonical_topics.citations: Mandell, Douglas, and Bennett 9th Ed, Ch. 21 (Mechanisms of Antibiotic Resistance); Jawetz 28th Ed, Ch. 28; Ananthanarayan 12th Ed, Ch. 10
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Bacteria confer resistance via 4 primary mechanisms: Enzymatic drug inactivation (Beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside acetyltransferases), target modification (PBP2a encoded by mecA gene in MRSA, vanA D-Ala-D-Lac in VRE), efflux pumps (MexAB-OprM in Pseudomonas), and reduced outer membrane porin permeability (OprD loss in Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae / CRE). NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamases hydrolyze carbapenems and resist clavulanate/tazobactam.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: MRSA strains resist all traditional beta-lactams including carbapenems because PBP2a has low binding affinity for beta-lactams; Ceftaroline (5th gen) is sole beta-lactam with PBP2a affinity.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Reflects the ancient Unani concept of 'Fasad-e-Taffuni' (Refractory Putrefaction resistant to standard balsamic antiseptics).

canonical_topics.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Granuloma Immunology & GeneXpert Diagnostics
canonical_topics.citations: Jawetz Ch. 23 (Mycobacteria); Mandell Ch. 249 (Tuberculosis); Ananthanarayan Ch. 34
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Obligate aerobe with mycolic acid lipid-rich cell wall rendering it acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelsen stain positive). Inhaled into alveoli, engulfed by alveolar macrophages, where it prevents phagolysosome fusion via cord factor and sulfatides. Cell-mediated immunity develops 2-3 weeks post-infection: CD4+ Th1 cells release IFN-gamma, activating macrophages into caseating epithelioid granulomas (Ghon focus + regional lymph node = Ghon complex).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: GeneXpert MTB/RIF is automated real-time PCR assay providing simultaneous detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance (rpoB gene mutation) within 2 hours.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Described with clinical precision in Avicenna's Canon as 'Dill' (Pulmonary Tuberculosis) recognized as contagious through shared breath and airborne dust.

canonical_topics.title: Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain & ATP Synthase Kinetics
canonical_topics.citations: Lehninger 8th Ed, Ch. 19 (Oxidative Phosphorylation); Harper's 32nd Ed, Ch. 13
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Electrons from NADH and FADH2 traverse mitochondrial inner membrane complexes I-IV (NADH dehydrogenase, Succinate dehydrogenase, Coenzyme Q-cytochrome c reductase, Cytochrome c oxidase). Proton pumping across inner membrane generates electrochemical proton motive gradient (delta-pH and electrical potential). Influx of protons through FoF1-ATP synthase rotor drives phosphorylation of ADP to ATP (chemiosmotic coupling).
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Carbon monoxide and Cyanide inhibit Complex IV (Cytochrome c oxidase), blocking ATP synthesis and causing lactic acidosis; 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP) uncouples proton gradient, generating lethal hyperthermia without ATP synthesis.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Biochemical molecular foundation of Unani 'Hararat Ghariziya' (Innate Metabolic Heat) and Ayurvedic 'Jatharagni & Dhatvagni' (Cellular Transformation Fires).

canonical_topics.title: Phenylketonuria (PKU) & Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism
canonical_topics.citations: Harper's Ch. 29 (Catabolism of Proteins and Amino Acids); Lehninger Ch. 18
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Autosomal recessive deficiency of hepatic phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) or its cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). Impairs conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine, causing neurotoxic phenylalanine accumulation and shunting into phenylketones (phenylacetate, phenylpyruvate) excreted in urine (mousy/musty odor). Manifests with severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, seizures, hypopigmentation (tyrosine is melanin precursor), and eczema.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Neonatal Guthrie bacterial inhibition test or tandem mass spectrometry permits early dietary phenylalanine restriction (medical formula), preventing cognitive decrement.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Manifests modern chromosomal substrate of inherited congenital diatheses (Mizaj-e-Khilqi) documented in ancient constitutional treatises.

canonical_topics.title: Clinical Toxidromes: Cholinergic, Anticholinergic, Opioid & Sympathomimetic
canonical_topics.citations: Goldfrank's Toxicologic Emergencies 11th Ed, Ch. 17 (Initial Evaluation of the Poisoned Patient); Parikh's 8th Ed, Ch. 22
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Constellations of vital sign and physical exam findings diagnostic of toxicological classes. Cholinergic (Organophosphates): DUMBELS (Diarrhea, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia/Bronchorrhea, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation) treated with Atropine + Pralidoxime. Anticholinergic (Atropine, Datura): Hyperthermia, dry skin, mydriasis, delirium, urinary retention ('Blind as a bat, mad as a hatter, red as a beet, hot as a hare, dry as a bone') treated with Physostigmine. Opioid: Coma, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression treated with Naloxone.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Distinguishing Sympathomimetic (Cocaine, Amphetamines) from Anticholinergic: Sympathomimetic patients present with profuse diaphoresis, while anticholinergic patients have warm, dry, anhidrotic skin.
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Directly matches Sushruta Samhita Kalpasthana's Sthavara Visha classifications and Avicenna's poison syndromes in Ilm al-Sumoom.

canonical_topics.title: Thanatology, Post-Mortem Interval (PMI) & Algor/Rigor/Livor Mortis
canonical_topics.citations: Reddy's Essentials of Forensic Medicine 35th Ed, Ch. 5 (Postmortem Changes); Parikh's Ch. 5
canonical_topics.high_yield_summary: Algor Mortis (cooling of body post-mortem, ~1.5°F/hour under temperate conditions via Glaister equation). Livor Mortis (post-mortem hypostasis/lividity): reddish-purple capillary pooling, appears 1-2 hours, fixes by 6-8 hours (does not blanch with thumb pressure). Rigor Mortis (post-mortem muscular rigidity due to ATP depletion preventing actin-myosin detachment): starts in small involuntary muscles of face/jaw (Nysten's law) at 1-2 hours, spreads to whole body by 12 hours, persists 12-24 hours, vanishes by 36 hours as autolysis commences.
canonical_topics.clinical_pearls: Cherry-red post-mortem lividity indicates Carbon Monoxide poisoning or Cyanide; chocolate-brown lividity denotes methemoglobinemia (Nitrites, Chlorates).
canonical_topics.classical_epistemic_note: Correlates with classical Islamic medico-legal coroner jurisprudence (Al-Tibb al-Shar'i) regarding irreversible cessation of Ruh Haiwani (vital respiratory/circulatory spirit).

key_volumes: Compound formulations arranged by pharmaceutical dosage forms

authorities.title: Qarabadeen-e-Jadid (قرابادین جدید)
authorities.author: Hakim Muhammad Kabiruddin
authorities.importance: Standardized modern compilation of classical formulations with metrology conversions into metric weights and clear indications.
key_volumes: Standardized recipes for modern dispensary and institutional practice

authorities.title: Qarabadeen-e-Najm-ul-Ghani (Khaza'in al-Adwiya / قرابادین نجم الغنی)
authorities.author: Hakim Najm al-Ghani Rampuri
authorities.importance: Renowned for bridging classical Mughal-era formulations with early modern pharmacognosy and regional botanical identities.
key_volumes: Comprehensive compound formulas, dosage modifications, and clinical commentary

authorities.title: Qarabadeen-e-Shifa'i (Tibb-e-Shifa'i / قرابادین شفائی)
authorities.author: Muzaffar ibn Muhammad al-Husayni Shifa'i
authorities.importance: Classic Safavid medical formulary heavily referenced across South Asian and Middle Eastern Unani compounding.
key_volumes: Electuaries, distilled waters (Arqiyat), and specialized powders (Sufuf)

authorities.title: Qarabadeen-e-Azam wa Akmal / Regional Qarabadeen Compendia
authorities.author: Hakim Muhammad Akmal Khan / Regional Compilers
authorities.importance: Crucial for identifying regional variations in drug nomenclature, traditional weights (Masha, Ratti, Misqal), and local excipient substitutions.
key_volumes: Regional South Asian variants and traditional compounding traditions

authorities.title: Unani Pharmacopoeia of India (UPI) — Parts I & II
authorities.author: Unani Pharmacopoeia Committee, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India
authorities.importance: Official legal and pharmacopoeial authority under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940. Defines identity, purity, TLC/HPTLC profiles, foreign matter, ash limits, and assay standards.
key_volumes: Part I: Single Drugs (Mufradat) — Volumes I to VI
Part II: Compound Formulations (Murakkabat) — Volumes I to IV

authorities.title: National Formulary of Unani Medicine (NFUM) — Parts I to VI
authorities.author: Ministry of AYUSH / Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM)
authorities.importance: Definitive national repository of approved compound formulations (Nuskha), legal batch compositions, method of manufacture, and shelf-life parameters.
key_volumes: Standardized proportions, excipients, and quality parameters for hundreds of classic compounds

authorities.title: Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM) Research Monographs
authorities.author: CCRUM, Ministry of AYUSH
authorities.importance: Clinical trial validation, standardization of single/compound drugs, ethnobotanical surveys, and safety validation of classical formulations.
key_volumes: Standardization of Single Drugs of Unani Medicine
Clinical Studies in Vitiligo (Bars), Rheumatoid Arthritis (Waja-ul-Mafasil), and Diabetes (Ziabetes)

authorities.title: Charaka Samhita (चरक संहिता)
authorities.author: Agnivesha / Acharya Charaka / Dridhabala
authorities.era: Classical Era (approx. 2nd Century BCE - 2nd Century CE)
authorities.importance: Supreme authority on Kaya Chikitsa (Internal Medicine), Tridosha theory, Dhatu physiology, etiology (Nidana), and extensive therapeutics across 8 Sthanas.
key_volumes: Sutrasthana (Philosophical foundations, diet, 50 Mahakashayas)
Nidanasthana (Etiology of 8 major disorders)
Vimanasthana (Dosage, clinical examination, epistemology / Pramana)
Sharirasthana (Anatomy, embryology, mind-body connection)
Indriyasthana (Prognosis and fatal signs / Arishta Lakshana)
Chikitsasthana (Therapeutics of clinical conditions)
Kalpasthana (Formulations and pharmacy for Panchakarma)
Siddhisthana (Management of therapeutic complications)

authorities.title: Sushruta Samhita (सुश्रुत संहिता)
authorities.author: Acharya Sushruta / Nagarjuna
authorities.era: Classical Era (approx. 6th Century BCE - 4th Century CE)
authorities.importance: Supreme authority on Shalya Tantra (Surgery), surgical instruments (Yantra/Shastra), dissection, Marmas (vital anatomical points), and reconstructive rhinoplasty.
key_volumes: Sutrasthana (Surgical training, instruments, caustic alkalis / Kshara, Agnikarma)
Nidanasthana (Surgical pathology, fractures, calculi, fistulae)
Sharirasthana (Anatomy, dissection methodology, 107 Marma points)
Chikitsasthana (Operative procedures, wound care / Vrana Chikitsa)
Kalpasthana (Toxicology / Agada Tantra and venomous bites)
Uttaratantra (Ophthalmology / Shalakya, pediatrics, internal medicine)

authorities.title: Ashtanga Hridaya (अष्टाङ्ग हृदय)
authorities.author: Acharya Vagbhata
authorities.importance: The most widely practiced and memorized synthesis combining the insights of Charaka and Sushruta into elegant, crystal-clear verse.
key_volumes: Sutrasthana, Sharirasthana, Nidanasthana, Chikitsasthana, Kalpa-Siddhi, and Uttarasthana

authorities.title: Ashtanga Sangraha (अष्टाङ्ग संग्रह)
authorities.author: Vriddha Vagbhata
authorities.importance: Comprehensive prose-and-verse compendium detailing all eight branches (Ashtanga) of Ayurveda with rich historical and therapeutic nuances.
key_volumes: Detailed exposition across all 6 Sthanas with prose commentaries

authorities.title: Bhela Samhita (भेल संहिता)
authorities.author: Acharya Bhela (Disciple of Punarvasu Atreya)
authorities.importance: Rare and foundational contemporary of the original Agnivesha Tantra; critical for independent validation of Atreya teachings.
key_volumes: Early therapeutic concepts and distinct perspectives on Alochaka Pitta

authorities.title: Kashyapa Samhita (Vriddha Jivakiya Tantra / काश्यप संहिता)
authorities.author: Acharya Kashyapa / Vriddha Jivaka
authorities.importance: The preeminent classical authority on pediatrics (Kaumarbhritya), neonatology, obstetrics (Prasuti Tantra), and gynecological disorders.
key_volumes: Phakka Roga (pediatric malnutrition), dentition disorders, Lehana (pediatric electuaries)

authorities.title: Madhava Nidana (Rogavinishchaya / माधव निदान)
authorities.author: Acharya Madhavakara
authorities.importance: Definitive classical authority on disease diagnosis, clinical stages (Shat Kriya Kala), five diagnostic tools (Pancha Nidana), and differential diagnosis.
key_volumes: Nidana, Purvarupa, Rupa, Upashaya, and Samprapti for over 70 disease entities

authorities.title: Sharngadhara Samhita (शारङ्गधर संहिता)
authorities.author: Acharya Sharngadhara
authorities.importance: Cornerstone text of Ayurvedic pharmaceutics (Bhaishajya Kalpana). Introduced detailed pulse examination (Nadi Pariksha) and refined pharmaceutical processing.
key_volumes: Prathama Khanda (Pharmacology, metrology, Nadi examination)
Madhyama Khanda (Kashaya, Svarasa, Hima, Phanta, Asava-Arishta, Bhasma preparation)
Uttara Khanda (Panchakarma procedures and ocular/nasal preparations)

authorities.title: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (भावप्रकाश निघण्टु)
authorities.author: Acharya Bhavamishra
authorities.importance: The supreme, most widely cited Materia Medica (Dravyaguna) encyclopedia in Ayurveda. Details plant taxonomy, synonyms, Rasapanchaka, and first documented Phiranga Roga (Syphilis).
key_volumes: Haritakyadi Varga, Karpuradi Varga, Guduchyadi Varga, Vatadi Varga, Dhatvadi Varga

authorities.title: Dhanvantari Nighantu (धन्वन्तरि निघण्टु)
authorities.author: Dhanvantari Tradition (Early medieval)
authorities.importance: One of the oldest and most authentic Nighantu codices; 7 Vargas classifying medicinal substances, properties, and classical synonyms.
key_volumes: Guduchyadi, Shatapushpadi, Chandanadi, Karaviradi, Amradi, Suvarnadi, and Mishrakadi Vargas

authorities.title: Raja Nighantu (Abhidhana Chudamani / राज निघण्टु)
authorities.author: Pandit Narahari
authorities.importance: Renowned for exhaustive botanical synonyms (Namakarna based on habit, habitat, morphological markers) and precise medicinal actions.
key_volumes: 24 comprehensive Vargas with deep botanical categorization and regional terminology

authorities.title: Kaiyadeva Nighantu (Pathyapathya Vibodhaka / कैयदेव निघण्टु)
authorities.author: Acharya Kaiyadeva
authorities.importance: Exquisite emphasis on dietary substances, wholesome vs unwholesome foods (Pathya-Apathya), and detailed actions of medicinal plants.
key_volumes: Aushadha Varga, Dhatu Varga, Dhanya Varga, Pakvanna Varga, and Vihara Varga

authorities.title: Bhaishajya Ratnavali (भैषज्य रत्नावली)
authorities.author: Kaviraj Govinda Das Sen
authorities.importance: The most widely consulted practical formulation compendium in modern Ayurvedic clinical practice; contains hundreds of definitive compound prescriptions.
key_volumes: Chapters dedicated to specific disease therapeutics (Jwara, Grahani, Prameha, Amavata)

authorities.title: Chakradatta (Chikitsa Sangraha / चक्रदत्त)
authorities.author: Acharya Chakrapani Datta (Commentator on Charaka & Sushruta)
authorities.importance: Pioneered systematic integration of metallo-mineral formulations (Rasa preparations) into general clinical therapeutics.
key_volumes: Practical formulations arranged disease by disease with commentary

authorities.title: Yoga Ratnakara (योग रत्नाकर)
authorities.author: Mayurasuri (Anonymous author tradition)
authorities.importance: First classical text to formally codify the Ashta Sthana Pariksha (Eightfold clinical examination: Nadi, Mutra, Mala, Jihva, Shabda, Sparsha, Druk, Akruti).
key_volumes: Diagnostic procedures and comprehensive drug compounding recipes

authorities.title: Rasaratna Samuccaya (रसरत्न समुच्चय)
authorities.author: Acharya Vagbhata (Son of Simhagupta / Rasa-Vagbhata)
authorities.importance: The quintessential masterwork on Ayurvedic alchemy and metallo-mineral pharmaceutics: laboratory construction (Rasashala), apparatuses (Yantras), crucible purification (Shodhana), and incineration (Marana).
key_volumes: Purification and Bhasma incineration of Parada (Mercury), Maharasa, Uparasa, and metals

authorities.title: Rasa Tarangini (रस तरङ्गिणी)
authorities.author: Sadananda Sharma
authorities.importance: Modern classic for standardizing Rasashastra processes, metric temperatures, and toxicological safety handling for mineral compounds.
key_volumes: 24 Tarangas detailing exact incineration criteria and quality testing (Varitaratva, Rekhapurnatva)

authorities.title: Rasendra Sara Sangraha (रसेन्द्र सार संग्रह)
authorities.author: Acharya Gopalakrishna Bhatta
authorities.importance: Practical bedside manual for clinical administration and therapeutic combinations of Rasa preparations.
key_volumes: Formulations categorized by therapeutic indication and dosage safeguards

authorities.title: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API) — Parts I & II
authorities.author: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), Ministry of AYUSH
authorities.importance: Official legal standards under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Prescribes macroscopic, microscopic, chemical assay, TLC/HPTLC fingerprinting, heavy metal limits, and microbial limits.
key_volumes: Part I: Single Drugs (Dravyas) — Volumes I to X (600+ monographs)
Part II: Formulations (Yogas) — Volumes I to IV

authorities.title: Ayurvedic Formulary of India (AFI) — Parts I, II & III
authorities.author: Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India
authorities.importance: Definitive statutory formulation book of India. Standardizes classical recipes from Charaka, Sushruta, Sharngadhara, and Bhaishajya Ratnavali for legal industrial manufacture.
key_volumes: Asava, Arishta, Avaleha, Bhasma, Ghrita, Taila, Churna, and Vati compound standards

authorities.title: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) Monographs
authorities.author: CCRAS, Ministry of AYUSH
authorities.importance: Preclinical pharmacology, toxicity profiles, clinical validation trials (AYUSH 64, AYUSH 82), and pharmacognostic monographs.
key_volumes: Evidence-based clinical efficacy reports, safety dossiers, and pharmacovigilance reports

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Jigar wa Meda (Hepato-Gastric Tonic & Anti-inflammatory)
primary_indications: Warm-e-Jigar wa Reham (Hepatomegaly & pelvic inflammatory congestion)
Zoaf-e-Meda wa Is-haal (Gastric atony and chronic diarrhea)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 7 grams twice daily with Arq Badiyan (fennel aqua) or lukewarm water after meals.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Clinical hepatoprotection via attenuating elevated ALT/AST, free-radical scavengers, and suppressing hepatic microsomal NF-kB cytokines.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Contains sugar base (Qiwam); prescribe sugar-free decoction equivalent for diabetic patients.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Dimagh wa Chashm, Daf-e-Qula (Cerebral Tonic & Anti-catarrhal)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.official_statutory_standard: NFUM Part I (1:16) & UPI Part II, Vol I

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Vatavyadhihara, Amavata, Sandhigata Vata (Anti-arthritic & Anti-inflammatory)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.official_statutory_standard: AFI Part I (5:7) & API Part II, Vol II

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Kasir-e-Riyah, Hazim, Daf-e-Nafakh (Carminative, Digestive & Anti-flatulent)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.official_statutory_standard: NFUM Part I (1:19) & UPI Part II, Vol I

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Musakkin-e-Waja-ul-Mafasil wa Daf-e-Niqras (Anti-gout & Anti-arthritic)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.classical_standard: NFUM Part I (2.42) / UPI Part II Vol I
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 1 to 2 pills (500mg - 1000mg) twice daily with warm water after meals.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Natural microtubule polymerization inhibitor (via colchicine fraction) suppressing neutrophil chemotaxis, inflammasome activation, and uric acid crystal-induced joint inflammation.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min) and pregnancy. Do not exceed prescribed dosage.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Munaqqi-e-Dimagh wa Daf-e-Suda (Cephalic Purifier & Anti-migraine)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.classical_standard: NFUM Part I (5.20) / UPI Part II Vol IV
primary_indications: Zoaf-e-Dimagh wa Basarat (Cerebral asthenopia & memory fatigue)
Qabz-e-Dimaghi (Sluggish elimination linked to cephalic heaviness)

key_ingredients.ingredient: Post Halela Zard (Terminalia chebula yellow rind)
Post Halela Kabli (Terminalia chebula black rind)

qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 10 grams at bedtime with 150ml lukewarm milk or water.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Neuroprotective through GABA-A receptor modulation, anti-inflammatory eicosanoid inhibition, and reduction of cortical spreading depression.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Mild laxative action due to Anthraquinones in Halela. Safe for long-term use up to 45 consecutive days.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Meda, Jigar wa Masana (Gastro-Hepato-Renal Metabolic Tonic)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.classical_standard: NFUM Part I (6.10) / Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb Book V
primary_indications: Zoaf-e-Hazm wa Nafkh (Dyspepsia, flatulence & delayed gastric emptying)
Salas-ul-Baul (Urinary incontinence due to renal atony)
Shaib-e-Mubakkir (Premature graying of hair from impaired metabolic heat)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 grams twice daily after principal meals.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Enhances gastric pepsin and brush-border disaccharidase secretion, improves splanchnic blood flow, and exhibits gastroprotective anti-ulcer properties.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Exercise caution in acute active peptic ulceration or hyperchlorhydria due to warm carminative spices.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.canonical_title: خمیرہ گاؤزبان عنبری جدوار عود صلیب والا (Khamira Gaozaban Ambari)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Mufarreh wa Muqawwi-e-Qalb wa Dimagh (Cardio-Cerebral Exhilarant & Neuro-tonic)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.temperament: Mo'tadil ba Hararat (Equable with slight warmth)
primary_indications: Malikholia wa Waswas (Cardiac anxiety, neurosis, panic predisposition)
Sur-at-e-Inzi'al (Premature exhaustion associated with nervous debility)

key_ingredients.ingredient: Abresham Muqarraz (Bombax mori silk cocoon extract)
Warq-e-Nuqra (Silver foil leaf / Chandi ka warq)

qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 3 to 5 grams once daily in the early morning on an empty stomach with Arq Gaozaban or milk.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Potent anxiolytic and cardioprotective action modulating central monoamines (5-HT & Dopamine), attenuating resting tachycardia, and combating oxidative ischemia.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Avoid high doses in severe hyperglycemia due to inverted sugar matrix.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Mufatteh Sudad-e-Jigar wa Mudirr-e-Baul (Hepato-Biliary Deobstruent & Diuretic)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 25 to 50 ml mixed with 100 ml lukewarm water twice daily.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Promotes bile acid excretion, reduces hepatic portal venous congestion, and enhances glomerular filtration via natural inulin and flavonoid glycosides.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Safe across all age groups; monitor fluid balance in patients with severe congestive heart failure.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Hazim wa Kasir-e-Riyah (Proteolytic Digestive & Carminative)

key_ingredients.ingredient: Papita Desi (Carica papaya fruit extract / papain)

qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 1 to 2 pills sucked or swallowed with water immediately after heavy meals.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Accelerates protein cleavage and gastric emptying through exogenous proteolytic papain, reducing functional dyspepsia symptoms by over 70% in clinical observations.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Avoid in patients with acute bleeding peptic ulcer disease.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Bah wa Habis-e-Mani (Urogenital Tonic & Spermatogenic Enhancer)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.classical_standard: NFUM Part I (3.18) / UPI Part I Vol II

key_ingredients.ingredient: Bhang / Tukhm Qinnab (Cannabis sativa leaf juice)

qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 125mg to 250mg once daily mixed in 5g Majun Aarad Khurma or with full-cream milk.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Engineered bio-compatible tin nanoparticle complex enhancing testicular Leydig cell testosterone secretion and inhibiting smooth muscle hyper-reflexia.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Mandatory statutory AYUSH Shodhana (purification); never ingest un-calcined or crude metal tin.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Asab wa Daf-e-Falij (Neuro-Stimulant & Anti-Paralytic)
primary_indications: Falij wa Laqwa (Hemiplegia, stroke rehabilitation & Bell's palsy)
Khadar wa Rasha (Nerve numbness, sensory loss & tremors)
Waja-ul-Mafasil Barid (Severe chronic arthritis with cold deformity)

key_ingredients.ingredient: Filfil Siyah & Filfil Daraz (Piper nigrum & longum)

qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 3 grams once daily after breakfast with warm milk.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Reversible post-synaptic glycine receptor antagonism facilitating spinal motor neuron signal transmission, accelerating post-stroke motor functional recovery.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: High clinical vigilance (Narrow Therapeutic Index); contraindicated in hypertension, epilepsy, and cardiac arrhythmia.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Meda wa Dimagh (Gastric & Ocular-Brain Tonic)
primary_indications: Bukharat-e-Meda (Gastric fumes ascending to brain causing dizziness)
Ziyada-e-Safra (Excess Yellow Bile secretion with acid regurgitation)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 10 grams at bedtime with water.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Suppresses central histamine and gastric acid over-secretion, reduces vestibular hyper-reactivity, and provides sustained neuro-ocular antioxidant protection.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Mild bowel regulator; exceptionally safe for prolonged clinical use.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Qalb wa Aaza-e-Raeesah (Cardiotonic & Neuro-Psychic Exhilarant)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.temperament: Mo'tadil Ma'il ba Hararat (Balanced with mild vital warmth)
primary_indications: Convalescence following acute infectious diseases (Typhoid, Measles)
key_ingredients: Marwareed Nasufta (Purified calcined Pearl / Mytilus margaritiferus)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 3 to 5 grams once or twice daily on an empty stomach with milk or Arq Gaozaban.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Rich in bioavailable calcium carbonate matrix, micro-trace minerals, and crocin flavonoids; exhibits anti-arrhythmic, neuroprotective, and free-radical quenching properties.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Contains sugar base (Qiwam). Diabetic patients require caloric monitoring.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.canonical_title: خمیرہ گاؤزبان عنبری جواہر والا (Khamira Gaozaban Ambari Jawaharwala)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Dimagh wa Qalb (Cephalic & Myocardial Tonic)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 3 to 5 grams in the morning with lukewarm milk or water.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Modulates central monoamine neurotransmission; silk peptides and borage flavones enhance cerebral perfusion and mitigate oxidative stress in hippocampal neurons.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Avoid during pregnancy due to trace Amber content.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Mubarrid wa Mufarreh-e-Qalb (Cardio-refrigerant & Antipyretic Exhilarant)
primary_indications: Thirst & burning micturition due to systemic Pitta/Safra excess
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 10 grams twice daily with cool water or Arq Gulab.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Alpha-santalol content provides central sedative, mild hypotensive, and anti-inflammatory effects.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Contraindicated in severe cold-dyscrasia asthmatic states.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Musaffi-e-Dam (Blood Purifier & Dermatological Depurative)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.temperament: Mo'tadil Ma'il ba Burudat (Mildly Cooling & Depurative)
primary_indications: Jarab wa Hikka (Pruritus, chronic urticaria & scabies)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 10 grams in the morning and at bedtime with water.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Fumaric acid esters and swertiamarin downregulate Th1/Th17 cutaneous inflammatory cytokines, promoting epidermal clearance in plaque psoriasis and eczema.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Excessive doses may cause loose stools due to trace senna.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Mushil-e-Akhlat-e-Salasa (Tri-humoral Purgative & Deobstruent)
primary_indications: Suda-e-Muzmin (Chronic headache linked to colonic toxemia)
Joint pain associated with metabolic waste accumulation
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 10 grams at bedtime with lukewarm water or milk.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Stimulates colonic secretomotor neurons via sennosides and turpethin resins; accelerates transit time without mucosal blunting.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Contraindicated in pregnancy, intestinal obstruction, and acute appendicitis.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Aaza-e-Batinah (Master Visceral, Stomach, Liver & Bladder Tonic)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.classical_standard: NFUM Part I (6.11) / Qarabadeen Kabir / Galenic Codex
primary_indications: Zoaf-e-Meda wa Jigar (Cold gastric atony & sluggish hepatic metabolism)
Zoaf-e-Masana wa Salas-ul-Bawl (Urinary incontinence, nocturia & bladder atony)
Daft-e-Riyah wa Nafakh (Chronic flatulence, abdominal distension)
Premature hair graying & geriatric physical debility
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 grams twice daily after meals with water or Arq Badiyan.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Piperine, gingerols, and cinnamaldehyde increase gastric mucosal blood flow, enhance digestive enzyme secretion (pepsin, amylase, lipase), and increase bladder detrusor tone.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Use caution in active peptic ulceration or severe hot gastric dyscrasia.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Qalb wa Meda (Cardio-Gastric Tonic & Mild Exhilarant)
primary_indications: Zoaf-e-Qalb wa Meda (Postprandial palpitations & weak digestion)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 10 grams after meals with water.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.modern_pharmacology_correlation: Combines polyphenols from emblica fruits and volatile terpenes from cardamom; promotes gastro-protection without inducing acid rebound.
qarabadeen_reconciliations.safety_and_precautions: Safe for regular use; well-tolerated in geriatric patients.

qarabadeen_reconciliations.therapeutic_category: Muqawwi-e-Meda wa Habis-e-Is-haal (Gastric Tonic & Anti-diarrheal)
qarabadeen_reconciliations.standard_dosage: 5 to 7 grams morning and evening before meals with water.

allopathic_drug_interactions.physician_clinical_advisory: CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT ALERT [CRITICAL_CONTRAINDICATION]: This botanical exerts pharmacodynamically active constituents with documented liability on hepatic Cytochrome P450 enzymes and/or ABC/SLC drug transporters. Attending physicians should review concurrent allopathic regimens for Calcineurin Inhibitor Immunosuppressants.

interaction_alerts.cyp_transporter_pathway: CYP3A4 Reversible Inhibition + Intestinal P-gp (ABCB1) Efflux Blockade
interaction_alerts.biochemical_mechanism: Berberine competitively inhibits CYP3A4 and intestinal P-glycoprotein, impairing presystemic first-pass clearance.
interaction_alerts.black_box_clinical_hazard: Surge in calcineurin inhibitor AUC by 2.5–3.0 fold, triggering acute nephrotoxicity, hyperkalemia, and solid organ graft failure.
interaction_alerts.physician_actionable_directive: Strictly contraindicated. If co-administered, mandatory daily C0 trough TDM; reduce immunosuppressant dose by 50–60%.
interaction_alerts.tdm_requirement: Daily Cyclosporine/Tacrolimus C0 trough blood concentration monitoring.

interaction_alerts.cyp_transporter_pathway: Hepatic CYP3A4 + OATP1B1 Hepatic Uptake Inhibition
interaction_alerts.biochemical_mechanism: Inhibition of CYP3A4-mediated statin lactone oxidation and OATP1B1 influx.
interaction_alerts.black_box_clinical_hazard: Plasma statin AUC elevated by ~70–90%, dramatically amplifying risk of statin-induced myopathy and fatal rhabdomyolysis.
interaction_alerts.physician_actionable_directive: Monitor serum creatine kinase (CK). Consider temporary statin dose reduction (e.g. Atorvastatin 20mg -> 10mg) or switch to non-CYP3A4 Pravastatin.
interaction_alerts.tdm_requirement: Baseline and 2-week serum Creatine Kinase (CK) and AST/ALT.

interaction_alerts.cyp_transporter_pathway: Renal OCT2 Transporter Competition + Additive AMPK / SUR1 Activation
interaction_alerts.biochemical_mechanism: Berberine independently activates AMPK and delays renal excretion of Metformin via OCT2.
interaction_alerts.black_box_clinical_hazard: Profound additive hypoglycemia and heightened risk of Metformin-associated lactic acidosis in elderly patients.
interaction_alerts.physician_actionable_directive: Intensify home self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG). Dose-titrate Metformin downward by 25–50% upon Berberine initiation.
interaction_alerts.tdm_requirement: Frequent capillary blood glucose logs (pre-prandial and 2h post-prandial).

authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Book II: Materia Medica & Simple Drugs (الکتاب الثانی فی الادویۃ المفردۃ)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: الدواء المطلق هو الذي يؤثر في بدن الإنسان بکیفیته فقط دون عنصريته، والمزاج حاصل من تفاعل الكيفيات المتضادة حتى تكسر سورة كل واحدة منها الأخرى وتستقر على كيفية متشابهة في جميع الأجزاء.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: دوا وہ شے ہے جو انسانی جسم میں اپنے مادی عنصر کی بجائے محض اپنی خاصیت اور کیفیت کے ذریعے اثر انداز ہوتی ہے۔ اور مزاج وہ کیفیتِ متشابہ ہے جو متضاد کیفیتوں (حرارت، برودت، رطوبت، یبوست) کے باہمی تعامل سے پیدا ہوتی ہے یہاں تک کہ ان کی تندی ٹوٹ جائے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: A true medicine is that which exerts its action upon the human body solely through its intrinsic dynamic qualities rather than mere material substance. The Temperament (Mizaj) is the unified equable state resulting from the mutual interaction of contrary qualities.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Ibn Sina establishes the distinction between food (Ghidha) which nourishes matter, and medicine (Dawa) which transforms physiological bio-energetic states via qualitative potency.

authentic_codex_folios.work_title: Kitāb al-Hāwī fī al-Ṭibb (کتاب الحاوی فی الطب)
authentic_codex_folios.author: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Zakariyyā al-Rāzī (الرازی / Rhazes, 865–925 CE)
authentic_codex_folios.historical_edition: Osmania Oriental Publications / Hyderabad Royal Edition (1955 CE) & Bodleian Codex
authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Volume I: Diseases of the Nervous System (جلد اول: امراضِ اعصاب و سر)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: الفالج إذا كان من بلغم غليظ سدد مجاري الروح في الدماغ، فإن علامته استرخاء العضو مع برده وضعف حسه، وعلاجه الاستفراغ بالإيارج والاستعانة بالدهون الحارة كروغن السداب وروغن الخردل مع تدليك الأعضاء.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: فالج (ہیمپلیجیا / فالجِ نیمہ) جب کسی گاڑھے بلغم کی وجہ سے ہو جو دماغ میں روحِ نفسانی کی گزرگاہوں کو بند کر دے، تو اس کی علامت عضو کا ڈھیلا پڑ جانا، سرد ہو جانا اور اس کے لمس کا کمزور ہو جانا ہے۔ اور اس کا علاج ایارجات کے ذریعے مادے کا اخراج اور گرم تیلوں (روغنِ سداب و سرسوں) سے مالش کرنا ہے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: When hemiplegia arises from thick phlegmatic congestion obstructing the pathways of the vital neural spirit in the cerebral parenchyma, its diagnostic signs are flaccidity of the extremity, coolness, and impaired sensation. The therapeutic protocol requires systemic evacuation using Ayarij followed by stimulating warm oleation and counter-irritant friction.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Al-Razi provides empirical case documentation of ischemic cerebral vascular accidents, detailing the vital distinction between upper motor neuron spasticity and flaccid post-stroke paralysis.

authentic_codex_folios.work_title: Kāmil al-Ṣināʿah al-Ṭibbiyyah (کامل الصناعۃ الطبیۃ - کتاب الملکی)
authentic_codex_folios.author: ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Majūsī (علی ابن العباس المجوسی / Haly Abbas, d. 994 CE)
authentic_codex_folios.historical_edition: Bulaq Imperial Edition / Munshi Nawal Kishore Urdu Royal Codex
authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Part I: Theoretical Principles & Vascular Dynamics (الجزء الأول: فی الأصول النظریۃ)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: العروق الضوارب إنما تنبعث من القلب وتنبسط بالحرارة الغريزية لتجذب الهواء النقي وتطرد البخار الدخاني، وكل نبضة مركبة من حركة وسكونين، وبعيار النبض يستدل الحاذق على قوة الروح وسلامة الجوهر.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: دھڑکنے والی رگیں (شریانیں) دل سے پھوٹتی ہیں اور حرارتِ غریزی کے ذریعے پھیلتی ہیں تاکہ پھیپھڑوں سے صاف ہوا کھینچیں اور دخانی دھوئیں کو باہر نکالیں۔ ہر نبض حرکت اور دو سکوتوں پر مشتمل ہوتی ہے، اور نبض کی پیمائش سے طبیبِ حاذق روحِ حیوانی کی قوت کا اندازہ لگاتا ہے۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: The pulsating vessels (arteries) originate directly from the heart and expand via innate metabolic heat to draw fresh air and expel smoky vapors. Every pulse wave consists of movement followed by two pauses. Through rigorous pulse appraisal, the clinician assesses the vigor of vital spirit and circulatory tone.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Majusi's accurate hemodynamic treatise predates William Harvey's De Motu Cordis by 600 years, describing the capillary exchange concept between arteries and veins.

authentic_codex_folios.work_title: Kitāb al-Taṣrīf li-man ʿAjiza ʿan al-Taʾlīf (کتاب التصریف لمن عجز عن التألیف)
authentic_codex_folios.author: Abū al-Qāsim Khalaf ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Zahrāwī (الزہراوی / Albucasis, 936–1013 CE)
authentic_codex_folios.historical_edition: Oxford Clarendon Press & Bibliotheca Arabico-Hispana (1778 CE)
authentic_codex_folios.volume_and_book: Treatise 30: On Surgery & Operative Instruments (المقالة الثلاثون: في الجراحة)
authentic_codex_folios.original_text_matan: لا ينبغي للطبيب أن يقدم على علاج بالحديد حتى يستقصي علم التشريح لأعضاء البدن، وأصول العروق ومجاري الأعصاب، كيلا يقطع عرقاً نافضاً أو عصباً محركاً فيحدث زمناً لا دواء له.
authentic_codex_folios.urdu_translation: طبیب یا جراح کے لیے یہ ہرگز جائز نہیں کہ وہ جسم پر نشتر یا لوہے (جراحی) کا استعمال کرے جب تک کہ وہ اعضاء کی مکمل اناٹومی (تشریح)، رگوں کی جڑوں اور اعصاب کے راستوں کو پوری طرح نہ جان لے۔ ورنہ وہ کسی خون کی بڑی نالی یا حس و حرکت والے اعصاب کو کاٹ دے گا جس سے ایسا لاعلاج نقص پیدا ہو جائے گا جس کا کوئی علاج نہیں۔
authentic_codex_folios.english_translation: No practitioner should venture into surgical interventions with iron instruments until he has mastered the exact anatomy of bodily organs, the paths of arterial blood vessels, and the tracts of motor nerves, lest he sever a major vessel or a vital nerve, causing irreparable lifelong paralysis.
authentic_codex_folios.scholarly_commentary: Al-Zahrawi establishes the universal imperative of anatomical training prior to surgery, introducing ligatures, catgut sutures, and over 200 surgical instruments invented in Cordoba.
